production.waterSource: Production water is drawn from Cursack Springs; specialist technical sources distinguish this from Cawdor Burn/process-water supplies.
production.malt: Unpeated malted barley; the distillery no longer operates floor maltings.
production.fermentation: Eight washbacks are used: six wooden washbacks and two stainless-steel washbacks. Established specialist sources report a long fermentation of about 68-70 hours, used to favour ester-driven fruitiness.
production.stills: Four copper pot stills: two wash stills and two spirit stills. The stills are tall with rising lyne arms, encouraging reflux and prolonged copper contact for a lighter, perfumed spirit.
production.maturation: Official Royal Brackla releases mature first in American oak before finishing in selected sherry casks including Oloroso, Palo Cortado and Pedro Ximenez styles.

houseCharacter: Royal Brackla combines long fermentation with tall, reflux-promoting stills to emphasise clean esters, orchard fruit and perfume rather than heavy sulphury weight. The distillation regime produces a bright, relatively light spirit able to carry assertive sherry finishing. American-oak primary maturation followed by sherry-cask finishing supplies the richer dried-fruit and spice layer associated with the modern house range.
cask23Narrative: Royal Brackla is a Highland distillery whose production is engineered toward elegance before the cask work begins. Long fermentation and tall, reflux-heavy stills favour a clean, fruity new make, while the current house range is then shaped through American-oak maturation and carefully chosen sherry finishes. That contrast explains why Royal Brackla can feel polished and perfumed at its core yet still carry substantial dried-fruit and spice richness.
